description: Dark rock grown through with ice: a crown, a mouthful, bladed arms, and more torn out of the ground at need.
lore: Above the snow line the ground turns crystal and stays that way, and the Rimeshard is what that ground does to a rock that stands in it long enough: dark plates iced through, a crown of blades off the skull, a mouth that is a row of them. When it wants more than it is wearing, it reaches down and tears it out of the ground — up there it and the ground are the same material, and there has never once been a shortage.

So the trade keeps one rule about it, bought dear and given away free: never above the line. Baited downhill onto ground that is merely ground, it spends its crown, then its shoulders, and cannot reach for more, and a patient crew can break the shape by dark. Above the line you are not fighting a creature so much as the ground it stands on, and the ground goes down a long way further than your patience.

Ask [[characters/8c41be1e|Hearn]] what was under [[lore/the_hole_under_the_mountain|the mountain]] and he goes somewhere behind his own face. Ask him instead about the Rimeshard he passed on the trail down and he will talk all evening: how it marked him, and let him by, and wanted nothing, took nothing, asked him for nothing. He calls it the most restful thing on that whole road. People who work the high ground use the same word, restful — and use it, as a rule, in the season before they come down for good.
gm_notes: Hearn's contrast is the point: the cave asked him for something; this thing asked nothing, and that is the only part of his journey he will narrate. Keeps the mountain at B7's hinted level — nothing about who or what is inside.
